All of this is in `src/tessel/views.py`.

**Building the view function**
- `View.to_view_func(cls, name, ...)` (line 86) is a classmethod. It returns a closure, `view(**kwargs)`.
- When `init_every_request` is true, `view` creates a new `view.view_class(*class_args, **class_kwargs)` per request. Otherwise it builds one shared instance up front.
- Either way, it calls `active_app.ensure_sync(self.run_view)(**kwargs)`.
- It then copies `view_class`, `__name__`, `__doc__`, `methods` and `provide_automatic_options` onto the function (lines 129-134) and applies any `cls.decorators`. The route registration reads `methods` from the function.

**Routing HTTP methods to `get()`/`post()`**
- `VerbView(View)` (line 138) is the subclass that does the per-method routing.
- `VerbView.__init_subclass__` (line 165) sets the class's `methods` automatically. It does this by unioning the bases' `methods` with every name from `http_method_funcs` (line 11) that the class defines, uppercased. So defining `get` and `post` gives `{"GET", "POST"}`.
- `VerbView.run_view(**kwargs)` (line 182) does the dispatch. It runs `getattr(self, request.method.lower())` and calls it through `active_app.ensure_sync`.
- `HEAD` falls back to `get` if there is no `head` handler. A missing handler hits the assert at line 190.

So the chain is `Hello.to_view_func("name")` → `view()` → `VerbView.run_view()` → `get()` or `post()`.
